findings.description: When ANSI stripping is triggered, the code calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text. That removes leading and trailing whitespace, not only the escape codes.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the output is redirected (not a tty) or color is disabled, and the prompt ends with a space, e.g. 'Name: ' or the confirm suffix ' [y/N]: '. strip_ansi alone removes the codes, but `.strip()` also drops the trailing space, so the prompt prints as 'Name:' directly against the user's input. Leading indentation and newlines are lost too. The output differs depending on whether stripping applies, and the title only promises ANSI stripping.
